offence_severity: Life imprisonment and two years rigorous imprisonment for the offence punishable under Section 148 IPC
physical_harm: The deceased was beaten to death with lathis
number_of_offences: Charged under Sections 148 and 302 r/w 149 IPC; finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court did not accept the testimony of the main witnesses PW10 and PW11 due to contradictions and inconsistencies in their statements, and questioned the fairness of the investigation.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW10 and PW11) as unreliable due to contradictions in their statements, their improving statements over time, and the lack of consistency in their accounts of the incident and attending circumstances.
bail_history: Accused are on bail. Their bail bonds are discharged.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 25.05.1994; Trial judgment: 30.03.1995; High Court decision: 24.10.2008; Supreme Court decision: 24.10.2019
legal_representation: Shikhil Suri, Adv. (A.C.), Ms. June Chaudhary, Sr. Adv., Mohd. Parvez Dabas, Uzmi Jameel Husain, Ms. Shilpa Saini, Shakil Ahmed Syed, Advs. for the Appellants; Rahul Kaushik, Ms. Bhuvneshwari Pathak, Ms. Shilpi Satyapriya Satyam, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR recorded after visiting the spot by the police; site plan prepared; investigation not fair
procedural_irregularity: The manner in which the site plan was prepared clearly indicates that the investigation was not a fair investigation
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction upheld; High Court: Conviction upheld; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside, accused acquitted
prosecution_argument: The prosecution relied mainly on the testimony of two eye-witnesses, PW10 and PW11, who claimed to have seen the accused beating Gajraj Singh with lathis. The FIR was recorded after the police visited the spot, and the witnesses were treated as credible eye-witnesses.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the testimonies of PW10 and PW11 are untrustworthy and contradictory. They also pointed out that the investigation was not fair, and many important witnesses were not examined. The witnesses had criminal antecedents, and there was enmity between the parties, which could have led to false accusations.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the prosecution must establish the guilt of the accused beyond a reasonable doubt, and that contradictions in witness statements and flaws in the investigation can cast doubt on the reliability of the conviction.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered the contradictions in the witness statements, the possibility of a concocted prosecution story, the presence of enmity, and the criminal antecedents of the witnesses.
